statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-68968 (GHSA-j4jc-cq9h-xrhr): in Apache Airflow before 3.3.1, the Backfill API's authorization dependency parsed backfill_id with int() while the route handler used pydantic's NonNegativeInt, so a value such as 1.0 was authorized against a caller-supplied Dag but acted on another Dag's backfill, letting a user with edit permission on any one Dag read, pause and cancel other Dags' backfills. Upstream fixed it in 3.3.1 with pull request 70889, backported to the 3.3 branch as commit 6fcae4e2b0aabd22b006659bc47139a124813865 (pull request 71090); it parses backfill_id in requires_access_backfill (airflow/api_fastapi/core_api/security.py) with the same NonNegativeInt type adapter the routes declare: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-j4jc-cq9h-xrhr, https://lists.apache.org/thread/f9zmw6xs5b4syhwzbl6fsxm4kf2632ol, https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/70889, https://github.com/apache/airflow/commit/6fcae4e2b0aabd22b006659bc47139a124813865, https://github.com/apache/airflow/releases/tag/3.3.1 . We unpacked every package built from the airflow source in the DHI Debian 13 repository (the airflow package), 52 versions from 3.3.0-0 to 3.4.0-11 for amd64 and arm64, and checked every download against the index SHA256. The dist-info metadata shows apache-airflow and apache-airflow-core 3.3.0 in 3.3.0-0 to 3.3.0-3 and apache-airflow and apache-airflow-core 3.3.1, 3.3.2 and 3.4.0 in every build from 3.3.1-0 on. We also searched the shipped Python sources for the fix: _BACKFILL_ID_ADAPTER.validate_python(backfill_id_raw) in security.py is absent from every 3.3.0 build and present in every build from 3.3.1-0 on, on both architectures. FIXED at 3.3.1-0.
